Confidence scoring assigns a qualitative reliability signal to a page based on source count, source authority, and staleness.

## Rationale

The score flags which pages deserve re-verification — it is not a truth score. It is assigned at creation and revisited when new sources touch the same topic. The distinction matters: confidence scoring signals reliability and sourcing quality, not correctness or truthfulness. A page can be well-sourced and still wrong; conversely, a poorly-sourced claim might happen to be true. The scoring serves as a maintenance signal: pages with low confidence should be prioritized for fact-checking and re-sourcing when possible.
